title: Grammar: Cause, result, purpose and condition: choose the relationship you mean
subtitle: B2 · Unit 7: B2 · Environment and public policy: explain causes and effects

steps.title: Cause, result, purpose and condition: choose the relationship you mean
steps.body: These connectors are not interchangeable. Parce que / en raison de give a cause; donc / de sorte que can give a result; afin que / dans le but de express purpose; à moins que introduces an exception. Purpose clauses with a different subject usually take the subjunctive (afin que le dispositif soit accessible). With the same subject, an infinitive is often smoother (dans le but de réduire les déchets). Ask: is this the reason, the result, or the intended goal? A proposal's intended result is not automatically a measured result.

steps.title: Cause, result, purpose and condition: choose the relationship you mean
rows: Cause
en raison de + noun
En raison du coût, le projet sera évalué.
Because of the cost, the project will be assessed.
Measured result
donc / de sorte que
Le bac était plein, donc les déchets ont été triés plus tard.
The bin was full, so the waste was sorted later.
Purpose, different subject
afin que + subjunctive
Le guide est simplifié afin que chacun puisse le comprendre.
The guide is simplified so that everyone can understand it.
Purpose, same subject
dans le but de + infinitive
L'équipe teste le système dans le but de réduire le gaspillage.
The team is testing the system in order to reduce waste.
Exception
à moins que + subjunctive
Le projet continuera, à moins que le budget ne change.
The project will continue unless the budget changes.

steps.explain: Afin que introduces a purpose clause.

steps.prompt: Which phrase gives a cause before a noun?
steps.explain: En raison de is followed by a noun and gives a cause.

steps.prompt: What should you distinguish in a proposal?
options: Its intended purpose and measured outcome
steps.explain: An intended purpose is not the same as an observed outcome.
